Reading · 1

Reading · 3
Colors swirl from light in the thinning film (thin-film interference), not paint.
Reading · 4
Sketching moving color stripes turns a pretty swirl into evidence of thinning.
Reading · 5
Surface tension pulls the film; a free bubble settles into a sphere.
Reading · 6
Bubbles pop when the film breaks from touch, dust, drying, or thinning.

WONDER DAILY AGE 8 · GRADE 3 · ANSWERS · 3 / 3

Four looks at a bubble

Soap Bubbles

Quiz 1. What's a bubble made of?
A soap bubble is a thin watery soap film wrapped around a pocket of air.
Quiz 2. Why can colors swirl?
Light reflecting in the thin film can make shifting color stripes as thickness changes.
Quiz 3. Why are free bubbles round?
Surface tension pulls evenly, and a sphere uses the least film for the air inside.
Quiz 4. What makes a bubble pop?
When the film breaks from thinning, drying, dust, or a touch, the bubble pops.
Outdoor or kitchen bubble play works. Keep mix away from eyes; wipe floors. Wonderers model looking and timing, not spraying faces. Humidity and recipe change how long bubbles last.
